rules: Every printed exhibit this paper announces is named by its running number at its own position: eight of the twelve figure rows name it in a 'the following Figure N ...' clause and four in a 'Figure N shows ...' clause, and only Figure 1 is cited on the page after the one that carries the chart [mention.style] [mention.lead_pattern] [mention.lead_pages].

The announcing sentence almost always breaks across a typeset line with the bare word 'Figure' at the end of one line and the number at the start of the next, so the printed grammar is 'The following Figure' / '4 provides a demo' rather than a single phrase [mention.lead_sentence] [caption.verbatim].

Figures sit below their artwork and the paper's figure captions are all of the form 'Figure N: <noun phrase>', six to sixteen words, one sentence, no unit, no variable and no conclusion, and five of the twelve name the factor being varied ('with MA(30)', 'with different ranges', 'in the first 3 periods', 'with different transaction cost rates', 'with Gaussian noise') [caption.numbering] [caption.position] [caption.words] [caption.conditions].

Five exhibits carry no printed number at all - the framework chart on p4, the indicator grid on p13, the memorandum grid on p23 and the two appendix charts on p25 - and each is recorded with caption_source none rather than given a number the paper never printed [caption.numbering] [caption.verbatim].

Only one exhibit in the paper is three-dimensional: the p17 stacked bar with extruded side faces and a drop shadow, recorded as perspective-bars. Every other plate is flat, and no plate anywhere prints a colour bar [geometry.three_d] [geometry.colorbar].

Panels appear only in the two ISO/Pro comparisons (two panels each, same family), the MSE heat map with its ACF and PACF (three mixed panels), and the transaction-cost plate (a line panel beside a bar panel); only the mixed plates are recorded as composite-panel [geometry.panel_count] [geometry.panel_layout] [geometry.family].

Grids are horizontals-only except the memorandum grid, which is the paper's only boxed table with vertical rules, merged cells and a vertically spanned stub; none of the six grids has a zebra stripe, a diagonal header or a footnote row [table.rule_style] [table.merged_cells] [table.zebra] [table.note_sentence].

The three notation grids of section 3 are one shape repeated: two columns, one header row and a symbol in the left column, three times over, each with its own bullet label instead of a table number [table.rows] [table.cols] [table.header_rows] [table.text_cols].

Exhibits are never given a table-like reading sentence: the figures are read by the paragraph that follows them and only Figure 1's reading sentence lands on the next page, so read_sentences is 1 wherever the paragraph reads the plate and 0 wherever the next paragraph starts a new argument [mention.read_sentences] [mention.trail_sentence].
